harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a local CA "OS Comparison Root CA" on node1 (RHEL 10) via openssl, installed its certificate into the system trust store using update-ca-trust, verified trust with `trust list` and `openssl verify` against the default trust store, issued and validated a test leaf certificate, then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted node1 via systemd-run-scheduled systemctl reboot (ack returned before disconnect), polled through the outage, confirmed a changed boot_id post-restart, and re-verified the CA trust anchor and openssl verification survived the reboot.
actions_performed: Installed openssl package on node1 (RHEL 10, none present by default)
Generated 4096-bit RSA CA key and self-signed x509 CA cert with CN=OS Comparison Root CA, 10yr validity
Copied CA cert to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ and ran update-ca-trust extract
Verified CA anchor listed via `trust list --filter=ca-anchors` and validated via `openssl verify`
Issued a test leaf cert signed by the new CA and confirmed it validates against the system default trust store with no -CAfile flag
Captured baseline boot_id and CA-trust health on node1
Scheduled and executed a single reboot of node1 via systemd-run + systemctl reboot, returning ack before disconnection
Polled node1 until reachable again and confirmed a new boot_id
Re-verified post-restart that the CA trust anchor and CA cert file persisted and are still trusted

evidence.summary: openssl genrsa/req created ca.key and ca.crt; subject/issuer both CN=OS Comparison Root CA confirming a self-signed root CA

evidence.requirement: CA installed as trusted system CA
evidence.summary: Copied cert to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and ran update-ca-trust extract; trust list shows it as an anchor and openssl verify -CAfile succeeds

evidence.requirement: CA is genuinely trusted system-wide (not just file presence)
evidence.summary: Issued leaf cert signed by the new CA; `openssl verify leaf.crt` with no -CAfile flag succeeded using the system default trust bundle
Captured boot_id 739c9792-... and confirmed CA anchor present via trust list count=1 before reboot
systemd-run scheduled reboot in 2s, command returned SCHEDULED immediately; follow-up check showed antrieb-reboot.service actively running the reboot
Node became unreachable during reboot (connection timed out twice), then came back with new boot_id e94ecbfd-... differing from baseline 739c9792-...
After reboot, trust list still shows OS Comparison Root CA as an anchor and openssl verify of the CA cert against default trust store returns OK, with fresh uptime timestamp matching the reboot time
